entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Sulpicius Camerinus Cornutus was a Roman politician and consul in 490 BC, playing a crucial role in the early days of the Roman Republic. He served as an advocate for the rights of the common people, often finding himself at odds with the aristocracy. His efforts to limit the power of the patricians and promote citizen participation in governance helped shape the development of Rome's democratic institutions.

As a prominent figure in 5th-century BCE Roman politics, Camerinus Cornutus' influence extended beyond his immediate peers. He was part of a larger trend of reformers who sought to redefine the relationship between citizens and the state. His legacy can be seen in the later reforms implemented by figures such as Marcus Tullius Cicero and L. Cornelius Sulla.

Despite his contributions to Roman politics, Camerinus Cornutus' own life remains somewhat shrouded in mystery. While we know he was a consul and held various public offices, few details have survived about his personal life or family background. This lack of information serves as a reminder that not all historical figures leave behind an enduring paper trail.

One lasting impact of Camerinus Cornutus' political career can be seen in the long-term effects it had on Roman governance. His efforts to strengthen the power of the people and limit the influence of the aristocracy paved the way for future reforms and helped cement Rome's position as a beacon of democracy in ancient Italy.

The 500-year gap between Camerinus Cornutus' consulship and his death in 500 BCE leaves us with few concrete statistics or lasting cultural footprints. However, it is clear that his actions had far-reaching consequences for the development of Roman politics and governance.
